messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] mixture model problem
parts:
The combination of this parameter declaration:

> real<lower=7,upper=19> mu[K]; // locations of mixture components

and these priors:

> mu[1] ~ normal(M[1],SD[1]) T[7,mu[2]-1.5];
> mu[2] ~ normal(M[2],SD[2]) T[,mu[3]-1];
> mu[3] ~ normal(M[3],SD[3]) T[,19];

is going to be problematic. The support of the sampling
distribution for any variable should match the constraints
in its declaration. If you don't initialize each mu[k]
in the truncated support, Stan can never move. But even if
you do, you will run into significant rejection.

But I don't think you want a prior or structure in the model
to keep the means separated --- the data should do that.

Your real problem, though, is the data declaration

> real y[N]; // observations

and sampling loop:

> for (n in 1:N) {
> for (k in 1:K) {
> y[n] ~ normal(mu[k],sigma[k]);

This samples y[n] from each of the mu[k]. You need
to code as in this model:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/master/src/models/basic_estimators/normal_mixture.stan

Basically, just get rid of the y[n] ~ sampling statement.
The sampling probability for y is implicit in the log_sum_exp
statement.

- Bob




On 3/29/13 4:47 AM, Bets wrote:
> Hey,
>
> I'm trying to construct a mixture model to analyse several distributions, but the output is never correct. I followed
> this converstation, but I still have values for Rhat or mu that are not satisfying
> (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/uE9O2DjSC80).

As I discussed near the end of the above thread, you won't
get R-hat values near 1 for the mixture components because
of identifiability issues. You could do something like sort
the means/variances (together), but unless the means are
well separated, this won't quite work either.


>
> This is a simplified version of one of my datasets:
>
> a1=jitter(rnorm(200,9,0.5),factor=10)
> a2=jitter(rnorm(500,12,1),factor=10)
> a3=jitter(rnorm(400,14,0.8),factor=10)
> a=round((append(a1,c(a2,a3))*2),digits=0)/2
> hist(age,breaks=30)
> priorfake=data.frame(mean=c(9.2,12.5,14),variance=c(1.2,2.8,2.4),n=rep(20,3))
>
> My model, adapted from the one from the manual:
>
> mixt <- '
> data {
> int<lower=1> K; // number of mixture components
> int<lower=1> N; // number of data points
> real y[N]; // observations
> real M[K]; //mean values prior
> real SD[K]; //variance values prior
> vector<lower=0>[K] alpha; // prior
> }
> parameters {
> simplex[K] theta; // mixing proportions
> real<lower=7,upper=19> mu[K]; // locations of mixture components
> real<lower=0> sigma[K]; // scales of mixture components
> }
> model {
> real ps[K]; // temp for log component densities
> sigma ~ uniform(0.2,2);
> theta ~ dirichlet(alpha);
> #for(i in 1:K){
> #mu[i] ~ normal(M[i],SD[i]);
> #}
> mu[1] ~ normal(M[1],SD[1]) T[7,mu[2]-1.5];
> mu[2] ~ normal(M[2],SD[2]) T[,mu[3]-1];
> mu[3] ~ normal(M[3],SD[3]) T[,19];
> for (n in 1:N) {
> for (k in 1:K) {
> y[n] ~ normal(mu[k],sigma[k]);
> ps[k] <- log(theta[k])
> + normal_log(y[n],mu[k],sigma[k]);
> }
> lp__ <- lp__ + log_sum_exp(ps);
> }
> }
> '
> K <-3
> chains <-2
> alpha <-rep(2,K)
> inits <- list(mu=priorfake$mean,theta=rep(1/K,K),sigma=rep(0.6,K))
> inits <- rep(list(inits),chains)
> mixt_dat<- list("alpha"=alpha,"K"=K, "N"=length(a), "y"=a,"M"=priorfake$mean,"SD"=sqrt(priorfake$variance))
> fit1 <- stan(model_code = mixt, data = mixt_dat, verbose = F,iter = 500, chains = chains,init=inits)
> fit1
>
> I added a prior for sigma and theta and tried to do the same for mu. When I just use:
> for(i in 1:K){
> mu[i] ~ normal(M[i],SD[i]);
> }
> all three peaks are almost exactly the same, and so doesn't match the prior at all. I want to have a certain distance
> between the peaks, so I added a prior for each mu seperatly (I hope I'm allowed to do this). In this case, theta does
> not converge and values for mu remain not logical. I tried this for several datasets, and there is a tendency of peaks
> being as close together as the prior allows. Can someone please suggest adaptations/corrections I can make to this model
> for it to work?
>
> PS: I also tried this, which didn't work out as well (overlapping normal distributions, not converging parameters,...):
>
> mixt2 <- '
> data {
> int<lower=1> K; // number of mixture components
> int<lower=1> N; // number of data points
> real<lower=0> y[N]; // observations
> real<lower=0> SD[K]; //variance values prior
> real<lower=0> D[K]; //prior for mean delta
> }
> parameters {
> simplex[K] theta; // mixing proportions
> real<lower=0,upper=4> sigma[K]; // scales of mixture components
> real<lower=1> age0; //location preceding mixture component (temp)
> real<lower=0.8,upper=4> delta[K]; //shifting component
> }
> transformed parameters {
> real <lower=1> mu[K];
> mu[1] <- age0+abs(delta[1]);
> for(k in 1:(K-1)) {
> mu[k+1] <- mu[k]+abs(delta[k+1]);
> }}
> model {
> real ps[K]; // temp for log component densities
> age0 ~ normal(9.248322,0.01); # mean,sd/sqrt(n)
> for (k in 1:K) {
> delta[k] ~ normal(D[K],0.1) T[0.8,4];
> sigma[k] ~ uniform(0.2,3*SD[k]);
> }
> for (n in 1:N) {
> for (k in 1:K) {
> ps[k] <- log(theta[k]) + normal_log(y[n],mu[k],sigma[k]);
> }
> lp__ <- lp__ + log_sum_exp(ps);
> }
> }'
>
> Thank you
>
